table_config.purpose: Describes how to generate content for a table. Coordinates are zero-based: row 1 and col 2 is returned as cells["1,2"]. The component-level instructions apply to the whole table. rows[] contains row-level guidance; a row instruction applies to every generated cell whose row matches that row index. columns[] contains column-level guidance; a column instruction applies to every generated cell whose col matches that column index. rows[] and columns[] do not create output cells by themselves; cells[] defines the configured cell coordinates. For each generated cell, combine the component-level instruction, matching row instruction, matching column instruction, and that cell's instruction. The cell instruction is the most specific, but row and column instructions must still be followed when they apply. Cell sizing fields are optional and use the same item-based vocabulary as text components. The strict limits are min_items and max_items (the number of items in items[]) and min_chars_per_item and max_chars_per_item (the length of each item): generated content must never exceed max_items or max_chars_per_item, and must satisfy min_items and min_chars_per_item, so shorten or compact content until it fits. max_chars is the strict total character budget for the whole cell — keep the combined length of all its items within it. target_chars, target_items, and target_chars_per_item are preferred sizes: guidance only, not limits — stay near them while always fitting within the strict limits. render_action controls output: only cells with render_action "render" can receive generated content; preserve or missing render_action means keep authored content and do not return that cell. content_policy only describes whether matching render cells are expected or optional; it does not make a preserved cell renderable. text_format controls item structure: plain uses exactly one item; paragraph, bullets, and numbered_list may use multiple items, bounded by the cell's item limits. Return only generated cell content keyed by "row,col"; never return table config, row/col fields inside cell values, schemas, explanations, or preserved cell content.

expected_content_schema.description: Expected AI output for a generic table component: generated cell content only, never table configuration. The response lists only the cells the AI fills, keyed by "row,col". Cell render actions, row/column content policies, sizing limits, and PowerPoint structure are defined by the component's tag_context.table_config.

cells.description: The table cells to fill, keyed by "row,col" (zero-based, e.g. "0,1"). Each key must match a render cell configured in this table instance's tag_context.table_config; do not return preserved or unconfigured cells. One key per cell; each value is an object with only an items array.

propertyNames.description: A cell coordinate key "row,col" (zero-based integers), matching a render cell from this table instance context.

items.description: Text items for this cell, obeying the matching cell's tag_context.table_config: use one item for plain text cells, one or more for paragraph, bullets, or numbered_list cells, and never exceed the cell's strict limits (the min/max item count and the min/max characters per item). Do not return schema, configuration, explanations, or preserved cell content.
